answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using trust-graph routing, where each agent is a vertex in an attestation mesh. Nodes exchange credit along interaction paths authenticated by compact falcon signatures, forcing attackers to incur a verifiable cost in scarce bilateral capital per identity. This avoids reliance on an ivory tower of centralized registrars. However, this model imposes severe onboarding friction on honest newcomers and cannot eliminate collusive bottleneck bridges.
